title: LETTER 3: Letter from Branch Manager to Head Office — NPA Report

blocks.content: Topic: You are the Branch Manager of Canara Bank, Pune. Write a letter to the Regional Manager reporting a sudden increase in Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) in your branch and requesting guidance.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Serves as an official internal document sent from the Branch Manager to the Head Office or Regional Credit Department detailing non-performing loans.
Requires a systematic structure including borrower details, loan limit, outstanding balance, date of NPA classification, and valuation of available security.
Outlines specific causes for default (e.g., market downturn, delayed payments, operational failure) alongside recovery steps already initiated.
Maintains an objective, factual, and analytical tone while seeking necessary approvals or legal sanctions for further recovery measures.

blocks.content: I am writing to submit the quarterly Non-Performing Asset (NPA) status report for our branch, highlighting key delinquent accounts and proposed recovery strategies.
Subject: Alarming Rise in Non-Performing Assets — Request for Guidance and Support

rows: Analytical & Managerial; seeks guidance and approvals
Legal & Firm; demands immediate dues clearance
Security valuation, provision status, causes of default, recovery roadmap
Overdue amount break-up, statutory notice under SARFAESI Act, legal warning

blocks.content: I write to bring to your urgent attention a concerning development in the credit portfolio of our branch. During the quarter ending 31 December 2024, our Gross NPA ratio has risen to 7.8% of total advances, compared to 4.2% in the same quarter of the previous year. This deterioration warrants immediate review and intervention.

The primary drivers of this increase appear to be threefold. First, a cluster of MSME accounts in the textile and garment sector has slipped into Sub-Standard category following severe disruption in export orders from key European markets. Second, three large agricultural borrowers have defaulted following an unprecedented hailstorm in November 2024, which destroyed approximately 60% of the standing crops in our lending area. Third, two personal loan borrowers have been identified as having furnished false income documents during the appraisal stage, and complaints have been lodged with the appropriate authorities.

I request your kind intervention to provide the following support: (a) sanctioning an additional recovery officer for our branch for a period of three months; (b) permitting One-Time Settlement negotiations for the three agricultural accounts in accordance with the Board-approved OTS policy; (c) guidance on whether SARFAESI action can be initiated for the MSME accounts given that all are secured by registered mortgages; and (d) arranging a forensic audit of the fraudulent personal loan accounts.
I assure you of my full cooperation and diligence in this matter. A detailed NPA statement for the quarter is enclosed herewith.

items: In descriptive bank exams, internal letters to Head Office must follow formal inter-departmental format, including Reference Number, Date, Subject, and structured tabular account summaries.
Candidates must remember the RBI definition of NPA (principal or interest overdue for more than 90 days) when explaining the rationale behind account classification.
Always include concrete recovery proposals such as SARFAESI action, DRT filing, or One-Time Settlement (OTS) recommendations in the letter body.

blocks.content: Examiner's Tip: Branch-to-head office letters must be professional, data-driven, and action-oriented. Use specific percentages and causes. Request concrete remedies. This reflects thorough banking knowledge.
